## What users will notice

- **Nothing, for almost everything.** List/create/get/close keep byte-identical response
  shapes, including the 200-with-`{}` missing-ticket quirk the legacy UI depends on, the
  1/2/3 priority aliases, and the no-pagination full dump.
- **Ticket closing stops stalling.** Today a slow SMTP provider holds the close request for
  up to 30 seconds and an outage turns closes into 500s *after* the ticket already closed
  (PB-001). After ED-001, the response returns immediately and the watcher email is queued
  durably. Same for the reset email (ED-002/ED-002b).
- **Reset tokens look different.** A long random token instead of 32-hex MD5 (PB-002,
  ED-003). Same 30-minute window, same single-use rule, same "invalid token" wall that
  refuses to say whether you were late or wrong.
- **Garbage requests get real errors.** Four inputs that crash legacy with a 500 (numeric
  title, unknown priority, float priority, non-object JSON body) return a 422 with a named
  error (ED-004a/b + the request_invalid convention).

## What users will NOT get (deliberately)

No pagination, no reopen, no slug uniqueness, no auth on internal routes, no removal of the
rate-limit bypass header — none of these are sanctioned by the problem brief. They are
either frozen behavior or open questions awaiting the owner (see decisions.md "Still open").
